column2: On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah,

direct me to a deed that, if I do it, will make Allah love me and people love me. He said: Renounce the world and Allah will love you, and renounce what people possess and people will love you.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by Ibn Mājah and others with ḥasan chains.

The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the most eager of people for every good and the quickest of people to every good. This Companion was eager to know what would bring him the love of Allah and the love of people, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ this question.
His words, “Renounce the world and Allah will love you”: he ﷺ made clear that the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is attained by renouncing the world (zuhd).

The best that has been said in explaining what is meant by renouncing the world is that a person leaves everything that distracts him from Allah, as the ḥāfiẓ Ibn Rajab quoted in his commentary Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/186) from Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī.
He said: “Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: In Iraq they gave us differing accounts of zuhd. Some of them said: zuhd lies in avoiding meeting people; some said: in leaving desires;
and some said: in not eating one's fill. Their words are close to one another. He said: My view is that zuhd lies in leaving whatever distracts you from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
What Abū Sulaymān said is good,
and it gathers all the meanings, categories and kinds of zuhd.”

His words, “and renounce what people possess and people will love you”: people are eager for wealth and the goods of this worldly life, and most of them hold on to what is in their hands and are not generous with it. Allah the Exalted said:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul—it is those who are the successful” [al-Taghābun 64:16].

They do not like someone who covets what they have or looks longingly at it; so when a person makes himself independent of them, he wins their admiration and gains their love, and when he gains their love, he is safe from their harm.
The Companions were eager for what would bring them the love of Allah and the love of people.
Love is affirmed as an attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
The servant's good lies in Allah's loving him.
Among the things that bring the love of Allah is renouncing the world.
A person's renouncing what is in people's hands is a cause of their loving him, so he gains their good and is safe from their harm.
